finding.claim: Mass assignment: PUT /me copies the entire request body onto the authenticated user object and saves it, so any authenticated user can set privileged fields (role, isAdmin, tenantId, id/ownerId, etc.) on their own account, enabling privilege escalation or tenant hopping. Also `__proto__` keys in a JSON body are own-properties set by JSON.parse, and Object.assign invokes the setter on the target, which can change the user object's prototype (limited to that object).

trace.note: PUT /me handler; only a user-attached req.user is assumed, no field filtering
Object.assign(req.user, req.body) merges all attacker-supplied keys into the user record
req.store.save persists the modified record, including privileged fields

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist of fields, no schema validation, and no role/tenant field protection in this file. The sibling route /me/profile at users.js:11 shows the intended allowlist (displayName, bio), so /me bypasses it. Only users.js is in the repo, so upstream middleware or store-level protections could not be checked. Authentication middleware that sets req.user is assumed to exist.

verdict.reason: users.js:5 does Object.assign(req.user, req.body) and users.js:6 saves it with no field allowlist or validation, unlike the allowlisted /me/profile at users.js:11-12, so any authenticated user can write privileged fields; no other files exist, so upstream guards could not be checked.
